statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of four representative unauthenticated paths. Authenticated browsing, playback, account settings, payment completion, help/media/jobs/shop subdomains, and logged-in cancellation were not covered because they require credentials, a commercial commitment, or use distinct properties.

page.framework: Netflix server-rendered acquisition UI with client enhancement
page.notes: The requested URL redirects to /gb/. Raw HTML is content-rich (90% coverage), while client JavaScript enhances forms, consent, and disclosures.

paths.description: Public UK landing page, representing acquisition, pricing, FAQ, consent, and the email entry point.
Sign-in form, representing authentication and account access.
First subscription step, representing the public pre-commit signup journey and plan framing.

findings.summary: The consent notice obscures core acquisition content on every tested entry surface.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the on-load banner covering the hero or form; on 360x800 it consumes roughly the upper quarter of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent treatment where legally possible, retain equally prominent accept/reject controls, and provide semantic light dismissal.

findings.summary: Consent and FAQ disclosure UI do not use the most appropriate native primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while screenshots show an overlay and the page contains accordion disclosures.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for a modal consent flow and details/summary for FAQ disclosure, preserving focus management and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: The page is fixed to a dark palette rather than explicitly integrating the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Default and dark-preference screenshots are byte-identical; computed color-scheme is normal rather than light dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for user-preference-aware surfaces, including form controls.

findings.summary: Public state and route changes have no authored View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules; the signup and login journey uses ordinary page swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained same-document or cross-document View Transitions for journey steps, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Several mobile controls and links fall below a comfortable 44 CSS pixel touch target.
findings.evidence: The 360px probe measured Sign In at 77x32, Learn more at 117x40, and footer links around 21px high, although keyboard focus was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS pixels using padding or pseudo-element hit regions without crowding the layout.

findings.summary: Empty form submission does not expose clear, inspectable error messaging or an announced recovery state.
findings.evidence: On landing and login forms, empty submission moved focus to the first field but yielded no role=alert/aria-live message or explicit error text in the probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, show concise field-level guidance, set aria-invalid, and announce the error summary through an aria-live region.

findings.summary: Mobile lab loading is outside the good LCP range and interaction readiness is delayed.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.1s, TBT 266ms, max potential FID 452ms, and TTI 16.9s; the trace recorded two long tasks and 114.6ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the hero LCP image, break up startup work, and defer consent, analytics, and non-critical application code until after the primary content is usable.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a large startup payload with avoidable unused code and an unprioritised LCP image.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.62MB transferred, including 1.29MB scripts and 680KB fonts. The largest script is 762KB; Lighthouse estimates 729KiB unused JS, and the LCP image lacks fetchpriority=high.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and conditionally load the acquisition bundle, subset fonts, eliminate duplicate reCAPTCHA loading, defer consent code, and mark the discovered LCP image fetchpriority=high.

findings.summary: The landing page heading hierarchy skips from H1 to H3.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies the “Ready to watch?” H3 immediately following the H1 as an invalid heading-order element.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic section headings in sequence, or render instructional copy as a paragraph when it is not a heading.

findings.summary: The viewport declaration prevents effective mobile zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found maximum-scale=1.0 in the viewport meta tag on home, login, and signup probes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and minimum-scale restrictions; use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 so users can zoom.

findings.summary: A third-party consent script logs a browser console error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured “Refused to get unsafe header X-OneTrust-IsBot” from otSDKStub.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or configure the consent SDK so it only reads CORS-exposed headers and does not emit runtime errors.

findings.summary: The page triggers DevTools issues and cannot use the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports cookie inspector issues and three BFCache failure reasons, led by Cache-Control: no-store on the main resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Review no-store use for anonymous acquisition pages, isolate truly sensitive responses, and resolve cookie inspector warnings.

findings.summary: Login and signup routes use the generic title “Netflix”.
findings.evidence: DOM probes show descriptive home metadata, but both /gb/login and /signup have document.title “Netflix”, which does not distinguish their purpose.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each public journey step a unique title such as “Sign in | Netflix” or “Choose your plan | Netflix”.

findings.summary: Public acquisition pages lack several indexing and sharing signals.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no canonical, no hreflang, no JSON-LD, and only an Open Graph description; /sitemap.xml redirects to NotFound. Raw HTML coverage itself is strong at 90%.
findings.suggestedFix: Add canonical and locale alternate links, publish a valid sitemap, and provide accurate Open Graph and Organization/WebSite structured metadata.

findings.summary: Active browser security policy coverage is incomplete and many cookies omit Secure.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no enforced CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Seven of nine observed cookies lacked Secure, while HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Move CSP from report-only to a tested enforcing policy, set Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and apply Secure to every HTTPS cookie.

findings.summary: Logging, consent, and third-party services create a large pre-choice network footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 52 of 54 requests and 2.53MB to origins other than www.netflix.com, including logging, OneTrust, Google reCAPTCHA, and geolocation; requests occur while the consent banner is still open.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat Netflix-owned CDN origins separately from external vendors, then delay non-essential logging, geolocation, and reCAPTCHA until needed or consented; batch essential telemetry.

findings.summary: The authentication surface exposes password sign-in without passkey evidence and omits the password autocomplete token.
findings.evidence: Login probe found an email field with autocomplete=email, a password field with no autocomplete value, and no navigator.credentials/passkey signal in loaded scripts; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete=current-password immediately and offer WebAuthn passkey sign-in or explain the phishing-resistant authentication path.

findings.summary: The global service sets language correctly but remains heavily dependent on physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: The page has html lang=en and uses some logical properties, but CSS inspection counted 389 physical left/right declarations and no explicit dir value.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir at the localized root and migrate layout-critical left/right declarations to inline/block logical properties, testing an RTL locale.

findings.summary: Image delivery is mixed: responsive sources exist, but dimensions and some sizing/format choices remain wasteful.
findings.evidence: Image probe found all four img elements without width/height attributes, two oversized images, and two legacy-format assets; measured CLS remained low.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions, tighten responsive candidates, and convert remaining photographic assets to AVIF/WebP where quality and support permit.

findings.summary: The anonymous landing page uses a disproportionate script, font, and external-service budget.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.62MB total, 1.29MB JavaScript and 680KB fonts; 2.53MB came from non-www origins, including consent and reCAPTCHA code before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt an acquisition-page budget, subset variable fonts, delay reCAPTCHA until form intent, and load consent/telemetry work at lower priority.

findings.summary: The steady-state heap is heavy for a mostly static acquisition page, although repeated FAQ use did not show an unbounded leak.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 686,116 nodes and 40.15MB self size. After ten FAQ cycles it rose only 0.4% to 40.31MB and DOM element count stayed exactly 1,088, so the concern is footprint rather than leakage.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the client bundle and object graph loaded for anonymous acquisition; keep the repeated-interaction test in regression coverage.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and includes oversized candidates.
findings.evidence: The image probe found no width/height attributes on four images and two images over twice their display width; doctype and charset are valid and observed CLS is low.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height attributes matching the selected aspect ratio and tune srcset sizes to the actual layout slots.
